tra_loi.Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies on the tower of the fortified town on the hillside in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780). The pictures don't show who the besiegers are, though the camps on the plain suggest a second force.
tra_loi.Q2: The Great Siege. The caption "1779 — The Great Siege" appears at frame 23, and armies then build camps on the plain beside the rock.
tra_loi.Q3: Not clearly shown. The pictures hint at a blockade, because ships ring the bay and sit offshore and there are long gaps with no friendly ships arriving. No food, famine or starving people are shown, so the hunger cause is not sure.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of many ships. A big group of sailing ships approaches the town from the sea in Jan 1780 (frame 47) and in Apr 1781 (frames 53-56). These look like relief fleets, but the pictures don't show them unloading supplies. Frames 13-16, with burning ships in Sept 1782, may show the besiegers' ships being destroyed.

tra_loi.Q1: Britain. A Union Jack flies over the castle tower on the Rock in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780), and the town stays fortified through the siege. The pictures don't show how it got there.
tra_loi.Q2: 'The Great Siege'. The caption '1779 — The Great Siege' appears at frame 23 (21 Jun 1779). Camps of many tiny soldiers or tents then grow on the land beside the Rock, and ships gather in the bay. So a long siege of the Rock by a land and sea force begins.
tra_loi.Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show food, empty stores or starving people. The siege seems to cut the town off: enemy camps on land and ships blockading the bay. People in the town are only hinted at as short of supplies (small figures on the slope and in the streets), so I can't say for certain.
tra_loi.Q4: A fleet of many ships sails in from the sea. It appears around 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47) and again on 12 Apr 1781 (frames 53-56), arriving at the town's harbour and walls. I read these as relief or supply ships, but nothing on screen says so.
